subject: Recap + next steps: deployment mode & cost model for Acme AI
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Patel <sanjay@acmeai.com>, Priya Menon <priya.menon@acmeai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@gmail>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@gmail>
Date: Mon, 24 Aug 2026 16:10:00 -0700
Subject: Recap + next steps: deployment mode & cost model for Acme AI

Hi Sanjay / Priya —

Thanks for the call today — good discussion. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can align on deployment mode and pricing.

Summary of needs from today's discovery:
- Expected steady-state: ~200 RPS (inference requests), with peak bursts up to ~800 RPS.
- Typical request size: ~120 tokens generated per request (median); some batches up to 512 tokens.
- Expected volume: roughly 500k generated tokens/day to start.
- Latency SLO: p95 < 300ms.
- Data residency: US only.
- Security: SOC 2 and audit logging required; potential requirement for VPC/private deployment later.

Deployment mode options we covered (high level):
1) Hosted API — fastest to integrate; per-token billing. Good for variable workloads and minimal ops.
2) Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity) — dedicated GPU pool with monthly commit; predictable throughput and lower effective per-token cost at scale.
3) Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) — full isolation, customer-managed networking; higher upfront costs and longer lead time.

Initial cost thinking (very rough):
- Hosted (per-token): $0.0006 / generated token (example model). At 500k tokens/day -> ~$300/day -> ~$109.5k/year.
- Dedicated (reserved): example 4-GPU reserved cluster = $20k/month commit -> $240k/year, but throughputs and model/quantization optimizations lower per-token cost significantly (effective $0.0002-$0.00035/token depending on utilization and batching).
- Private (on-prem): one-time infra + software + support (TCO varies widely); typically favorable for very large predictable usage or regulatory requirements.

Next steps I recommend:
1) We’ll send a short cost model spreadsheet with Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private scenarios (I will attach).
2) If you’re leaning Dedicated, we’ll model a 12 vs 36 month commit and show break-even vs Hosted.
3) Schedule a 30-min pricing + infra deep-dive with our solutions architect to go over sequence lengths, KV cache expectations, and burst behavior.

Action items:
- Aditya: share detailed cost model and comparison (attached) — today.
- Sanjay/Priya: confirm whether you want a Dedicated baseline (12/36 month) and any procurement constraints (PO, billing cadence).
- Marissa/Neha: jump in on technical follow-ups and SOC 2 evidence.

Attachments: redwood-dedicated-pricing.xlsx (spreadsheet), redwood-deployment-comparison.pdf

Thanks —
Aditya Rao
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
aditya@redwood.com | (415) 555-0123

From: Sanjay Patel <sanjay@acmeai.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Menon <priya.menon@acmeai.com>, procurement@acmeai.com
Date: Mon, 24 Aug 2026 17:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap + next steps: deployment mode & cost model for Acme AI

Thanks, Aditya — helpful recap. A couple clarifications from our side:
- The 500k token/day number is our conservative estimate; if we include retries and embeddings we could be closer to ~750k tokens/day within Q1.
- Given latency and residency requirements, the team is currently leaning towards Dedicated (reserved capacity) to avoid burst throttling and get predictable latency.
- Procurement: we prefer 12- or 24-month commits; need details on refundability and exit terms.

Can you include a Dedicated baseline (12/24 month) with effective per-token pricing and an expected utilization assumption? Also confirm whether Dedicated supports VPC peering for audit logs and whether Redwood can provide SOC 2 evidence.

— Sanjay
Head of AI Engineering, Acme AI

From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Patel <sanjay@acmeai.com>, Priya Menon <priya.menon@acmeai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@gmail>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@gmail>
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap + next steps: deployment mode & cost model for Acme AI

Hi Sanjay / Priya —

Attached is the cost model spreadsheet (redwood-dedicated-pricing.xlsx) and a short comparison PDF. Highlights pulled from the model (assumptions: 500k tokens/day baseline; 80% utilization for Dedicated cluster; average seq length 150 tokens):

Hosted (per-token) — baseline:
- Price (example): $0.0006 / generated token
- 500k tokens/day -> $300/day -> $109,500 / year
- Pros: no commit, simple billing; Cons: higher unit cost at scale, potential rate limits during large bursts unless on paid tier.

Dedicated (reserved commit) — 4-GPU example:
- Commit: $20,000 / month (example) -> $240k / year
- At 80% utilization and batching, effective cost ~ $0.00025 / token -> for 500k tokens/day equivalent cost ~ $45k/year in compute-equivalent (note committed price > compute line due to reserved infra + support) but provides guaranteed throughput, lower p95 latency, and improved economics as volume grows.
- Break-even vs Hosted at ~1.2M tokens/day (depending on commit length and discounts).
- 12 vs 24 vs 36 month: deeper discounts at 24/36 months (we show 10-18% incremental discount for longer commits in the spreadsheet).

Private / On-prem:
- One-time infra + license + support; not typically cost-effective until sustained multi-million token/day usage or strict regulatory needs.

Other notes:
- Autoscaling & intelligent batching: Dedicated can include burst buffer capacity and autoscaling policies; we model 2x burst allowance for short periods.
- Caching: if you have high prefix reuse, KV cache can reduce effective generated tokens by ~15-30% (share any prompt overlap stats if available).
- Quantization: switching to int8/quantized variants can cut GPU costs ~20-40% depending on model and accuracy tolerance.

Next steps / ask:
1) Please confirm which commit term you want modeled (12 vs 24 vs 36).
2) Share a more detailed token profile (seq length distribution, embedding use, cache hit assumptions) so we can refine the model.
3) If you want to proceed with Dedicated, we should schedule a 30-min session with our infra lead (Marissa) this week — propose Wed 8/26 10:00am PT or Thu 8/27 2:00pm PT.

I’ll also loop in Contracts if Procurement needs standard T&Cs for PO processing.

Regards,
Aditya

From: Priya Menon <priya.menon@acmeai.com>

Thanks — received the spreadsheet. A few procurement questions before we schedule:
- Contract length options: can you send standard language for 12 and 24 month commits? Any early-exit fees?
- Billing: monthly arrears invoicing preferred; do you support net-30?
- Refundability: are unused committed credits refundable or convertible to overage credits?
- PO requirements / vendor setup: what info do you need to set Redwood up in our vendor system?

If you can send a note listing required vendor fields and a copy of the T&Cs for 12/24-month options, we can kick off vendor setup in parallel.

Thanks,
Priya Menon
Senior Procurement Manager, Acme AI

Looping in a few technical points from the Dedicated POV:
- Please share sequence length distribution (P50/P95) and percent of requests that are embedding vs generation — this materially changes compute and batch sizing.
- Caching assumptions: if UNIFORM prefix reuse is high we should model 20-30% token savings.
- Autoscale policy: recommend a baseline commit sized for 95th percentile steady throughput + 2x short-term burst buffer.
- For procurement: committed discounts tier with 12/24 month terms; we can provide standard PO/vendor fields and a draft SOW.

Proposed immediate action: 30-min infra deep-dive (Marissa + Neha + your infra lead) to refine cost model. I’m available Wed 8/26 10:00am PT.

-Marissa
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
